original_value: Recently, egocentric activity recognition has attracted considerable attention in the pattern recognition and artificial intelligence communities because of its wide applicability in medical care, smart homes, and security monitoring. In this study, we developed and implemented a deep-learning-based hierarchical fusion framework for the recognition of egocentric activities of daily living (ADLs) in a wearable hybrid sensor system comprising motion sensors and cameras. Long short-term memory (LSTM) and a convolutional neural network are used to perform egocentric ADL recognition based on motion sensor data and photo streaming in different layers, respectively. The motion sensor data are used solely for activity classification according to motion state, while the photo stream is used for further specific activity recognition in the motion state groups. Thus, both motion sensor data and photo stream work in their most suitable classification mode to significantly reduce the negative influence of sensor differences on the fusion results. Experimental results show that the proposed method not only is more accurate than the existing direct fusion method (by up to 6%) but also avoids the time-consuming computation of optical flow in the existing method, which makes the proposed algorithm less complex and more suitable for practical application.

result.paraphrase: Recently, egocentric activity recognition has drawn substantial interest from the pattern recognition and artificial intelligence communities due to its broad usefulness in medical care, smart homes, and security monitoring. In this study, we designed and implemented a deep-learning-based hierarchical fusion framework to recognize egocentric activities of daily living (ADLs) using a wearable hybrid sensor system made up of motion sensors and cameras. Long short-term memory (LSTM) and a convolutional neural network are employed at different layers to recognize egocentric ADLs from motion sensor data and photo streaming, respectively. Motion sensor data are used only to classify activities by motion state, whereas the photo stream is used for more detailed recognition within the motion-state groups. In this way, both motion sensor data and the photo stream operate in their most appropriate classification mode, greatly reducing the adverse impact of sensor differences on the fusion results. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method is not only more accurate than the existing direct fusion method by up to 6% but also eliminates the time-consuming optical flow computation used in the existing method, making the proposed algorithm less complex and more practical for real-world use.
